introduction: On this Sunday, the prophet Nathan confronts King David with his sin, and David says, I have sinned against the Lord. In the Gospel, a woman known as a sinner washes Jesus' feet with her tears, and he says that her many sins are forgiven because she has shown great love. Paul says, I live, no longer I, but Christ lives in me. Let us bring our sins to Jesus and receive his forgiveness.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, blessed are those whose sins are forgiven. Let us bring our prayers to the God of mercy.
intentions: For the Church: that she may welcome sinners with the compassion of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are weighed down by guilt: that they may confess their sins and know the joy of forgiveness. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who judge others harshly: that they may recognize their own need of mercy. Let us pray to the Lord.
For women who serve the Church and the poor, often unseen: that God may bless their generosity. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that, forgiven much, we may love much. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Merciful Father, you forgive those who confess their sins. Give us hearts that know our need of you, and let our love grow in gratitude for your mercy. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: She loved much
reflection.body:
King David has committed adultery with Bathsheba and arranged for her husband Uriah to be killed. The prophet Nathan comes and confronts him: "You are the man!" He reminds David of everything God had given him and asks, "Why have you despised the LORD's word?" David does not make excuses. He says, "I have sinned against the LORD." And Nathan answers, "The LORD also has put away your sin." The psalm sings the relief of being forgiven: "I acknowledged my sin to you... and you forgave the iniquity of my sin."

In the Gospel, Jesus is a guest at the house of Simon the Pharisee. A woman "who was a sinner" comes in. She stands behind Jesus, weeping, wets his feet with her tears, wipes them with her hair, kisses them and anoints them. Simon thinks to himself that if Jesus were a prophet, he would know what kind of woman she is.

Jesus tells him a short story about two debtors, one owing much and one little. Both are forgiven. "Which of them therefore will love him most?" Simon answers correctly. Then Jesus turns to the woman and contrasts her welcome with Simon's: no water for his feet, no kiss, no oil. "Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But one to whom little is forgiven, loves little." He tells her, "Your faith has saved you. Go in peace."

The danger is to be like Simon, thinking we need little forgiveness. Those who know how much they have been forgiven love the most.

Paul describes the new life that forgiveness brings: "it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me." He lives "by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me."

This week, be honest with God about your sins, as David was. Go to confession. Then let your love grow out of gratitude.
